Master ChemoInfo at the University of Strasbourg trains chemoinformatics specialists at the interface of chemistry and computing — a niche with strong pharma and materials demand. The current selection procedure covers the 2026-2028 intake, which the consortium has confirmed will run without Erasmus Mundus scholarships.

Programme Highlights

  • Strasbourg's chemoinformatics tradition with industry and EU-research links
  • Selection-procedure page carries the live admission steps
  • 2026-2028 intake confirmed without an EMJM scholarship
  • Graduates enter pharma informatics, computational chemistry and data roles

Who Should Apply

Chemistry, biochemistry and computer science graduates with programming skills are the natural fit; motivation for the chemistry-data interface matters.

Funding and Costs

The consortium has announced that the 2026-2028 student intake will run without an Erasmus Mundus scholarship; other funding options are listed on the scholarships page. Confirm the exact funding package on the official page before applying.

Deadline and How to Apply

Follow the selection-procedure page for the current round and check the scholarships page for alternative funding. Key deadline information: Admission round for the live intake per the official selection-procedure page (the 2026-2028 intake runs without a scholarship).
